question: Which mineral is especially important for growing and building white blood cells to fight infections?

options.A: Potassium
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Zinc
options.D: Sodium

explanation: You got it! Zinc plays a huge role in helping your immune cells multiply and do their job when an infection tries to take hold. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T13#GNS313_U2_T13_h2)

question: A patient on tiopronin calls reporting a sudden sore throat, fever, and skin rash. What should you advise?

options.A: Suggest taking an over-the-counter antihistamine and doubling the evening water intake
options.B: Tell the patient this is a normal harmless side effect that will resolve in a few days
options.C: Advise the patient to stop the medication and report to the clinic immediately for lab work
options.D: Recommend waiting until the next scheduled routine appointment next month

explanation: Fever, sore throat, and rash can be warning signs of a serious reaction or blood issue. It's always best to pause the drug and have the medical team check them right away! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T4#GNS223_U8_T4_h6)

question: Which chemical group includes volatile liquids like acetone that can affect your nervous system when breathed in?

options.A: Corrosives
options.B: Solvents
options.C: Sensitizers
options.D: Carcinogens

explanation: Solvents evaporate easily into the air. When we breathe them in, they can travel through our system and sometimes affect our neurological function. Good to know for safe lab practices! [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h2)

question: What is the main focus of 'internal validity' in a research study?

options.A: Proving that the treatment actually caused the change in the patient
options.B: Checking if the lab thermometer was working well
options.C: Counting how many student nurses helped collect data
options.D: Seeing if the results apply to patients in other countries

explanation: Internal validity is all about cause and effect inside the study. Did our nursing intervention really cause that improvement, or was it something else? [learn more](GNS224_U1_T26#GNS224_U1_T26_h2)

question: What is the most common and trusted way to sterilize metal surgical tools?

options.A: Boiling in water for twenty minutes
options.B: Steam under pressure in an autoclave
options.C: Ultraviolet radiation in a glass cabinet
options.D: Immersion in liquid bleach solution

explanation: The autoclave is the workhorse of the CSSD! Using high-pressure steam is fast, affordable, and extremely reliable for metal instruments. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h5)

question: What is the main goal of pediatric home health care?

options.A: Maintaining the child's health while keeping the family together
options.B: Training the child to live completely independently from adults
options.C: Reducing the cost of hospital building maintenance and upkeep
options.D: Replacing the parents as the primary decision-makers for care

explanation: You got this! Home care brings medical support right into a natural setting, helping the child stay healthy while keeping the whole family close together. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h1)

question: What is a common misconception about mental illness that fuels community stigma?

options.A: Knowing that counseling and medication help recovery
options.B: Believing it is caused by curses, witchcraft, or personal moral failure
options.C: Understanding it as a treatable medical condition affecting brain chemistry
options.D: Recognizing that stress can trigger episodes in anyone

explanation: False beliefs attributing mental illness to supernatural curses or weakness often lead to harsh discrimination and delay proper medical treatment. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h6)

question: A patient with a leg cast has severe pain, and their toes look pale and feel cool. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Perform a complete neurovascular assessment and notify the physician immediately.
options.B: Remove the cast immediately using an electric cutting saw at the bedside.
options.C: Reassure the patient that this is a completely normal reaction to a cast.
options.D: Administer a stronger sleeping tablet and wait until the morning shift.

explanation: Pale, cool toes and severe pain are red flags! They mean blood flow or nerves might be squeezed too tight by the cast. Quick assessment and calling the doctor can save the limb. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T4#GNS112_U7_T4_h3)

question: Why is discussing the realities of life support important during advance care planning?

options.A: It reduces the amount of paperwork nurses must file in the chart
options.B: It prevents family members from ever disagreeing with the doctor
options.C: It helps patients give truly informed consent for what they want or reject
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will live longer in the hospital

explanation: Patients need to know what procedures like CPR or ventilation actually involve so their choices are genuinely informed. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why do hospitals team up with legal aid groups and local shelters when caring for survivors?

options.A: To reduce the number of follow-up clinic visits required
options.B: To provide comprehensive support that addresses safety, housing, and justice
options.C: To transfer all medical responsibilities away from the nursing staff
options.D: To ensure that the hospital makes a profit from court fees

explanation: You got it! Healing takes more than medicine—teamwork helps survivors find safety, shelter, and justice all in one go. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T23#GNS225_U5_T23_h6)

question: What is the correct order for examining a patient's tummy (abdomen)?

options.A: Inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation
options.B: Palpation, percussion, auscultation, inspection
options.C: Auscultation, inspection, palpation, percussion
options.D: Percussion, palpation, inspection, auscultation

explanation: Always listen (auscultate) before you touch or press! Pressing first can change the natural bowel sounds and mess up your assessment. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h3)

question: What long-term heart problem often develops from chronic, untreated severe anemia?

options.A: Primary pulmonary hypertension
options.B: High-output heart failure
options.C: Chronic deep vein thrombosis
options.D: Peripheral artery disease

explanation: Imagine running a car engine at top speed every single day—eventually, it wears out. The heart muscle gets exhausted from constantly overworking to pump oxygen-poor blood, leading to heart failure. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T14#GNS311_U2_T14_h5)

question: You touch a hot pot in the clinical kitchen and instantly pull your hand back. Which fibers carried the signal from your CNS out to your hand muscles?

options.A: Sensory fibers
options.B: Efferent fibers
options.C: Receptor fibers
options.D: Afferent fibers

explanation: E-fferent exits the brain with instructions (think 'E' for exit). Quick reflexes keep future nurses safe! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the most important assessment to do before giving a patient an anti-spasmodic drug?

options.A: Testing the patient's grip strength in both hands
options.B: Measuring the circumference of the patient's neck
options.C: Checking the patient's visual acuity using a reading chart
options.D: Evaluating bowel sounds and the nature of abdominal pain

explanation: You always want to know what their pain and tummy sounds are like *before* giving the drug so you can tell if it's safe and if it actually helps them. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T4#GNS223_U3_T4_h6)

question: Roughly how long does the complete cycle of spermatogenesis take in humans?

options.A: About 6 to 9 months
options.B: Exactly 14 days
options.C: About 64 to 74 days
options.D: Exactly 28 days

explanation: The entire transformation from an immature germ cell to a mature spermatozoon takes approximately two to two and a half months. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of having good sanitation facilities?

options.A: Safe disposal of human waste
options.B: Production of clean drinking water
options.C: Elimination of flying insect pests
options.D: Reduction of indoor air pollution

explanation: Great job! Sanitation is all about making sure human waste is handled safely so it doesn't contaminate our environment or spread disease. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h2)

question: What is the clinical name for the bulging, wide-eyed look seen in Graves' disease?

options.A: Acromegaly
options.B: Acanthosis
options.C: Exophthalmos
options.D: Hirsutism

explanation: Exophthalmos happens when the immune system causes inflammation and fluid buildup right behind the eyeballs, pushing them forward. Great word to add to your nursing vocabulary! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T3#GNS222_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is a good alternative for severe hot flashes if a patient cannot take hormone therapy?

options.A: High-dose systemic testosterone injections
options.B: Strict fluid restriction during the evening hours
options.C: Low-dose non-hormonal neuromodulators like select SSRIs
options.D: Immediate surgical removal of the adrenal glands

explanation: Certain non-hormonal medications help calm the brain's thermostat to relieve hot flashes safely when hormones aren't an option. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T15#GNS121_U5_T15_h6)

question: Why is it important to talk about pain management before the patient takes misoprostol?

options.A: Pain medications must be taken to prevent allergic reactions to the drug
options.B: Analgesics speed up the absorption of the hormone in the stomach lining
options.C: Misoprostol causes strong uterine contractions that lead to significant cramping
options.D: Pain medication stops the excessive bleeding that occurs right away

explanation: Cramping is a very normal part of the process because the uterus is working hard to empty. Planning ahead for pain relief keeps our patients comfortable! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T012#GNS226_U5_T012_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of conducting a physical stock audit on a hospital ward?

options.A: To test the clinical skills of newly employed nurses
options.B: To compare actual items on the shelf with recorded inventory
options.C: To clean out the dust from the medication store cupboards
options.D: To dispose of all old equipment regardless of expiry date

explanation: Stock audits involve counting what is physically present to match it with what the logbook says should be there. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four central concepts in the nursing metaparadigm?

options.A: Medication
options.B: Health
options.C: Environment
options.D: Person

explanation: Easy to remember: the four pillars are Person, Environment, Health, and Nursing. Medication is just a tool we use, not a core pillar! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main job of the 'memory cells' created when someone gets vaccinated?

options.A: To permanently alter the person's genetic DNA structure
options.B: To destroy healthy tissue to make space for white blood cells
options.C: To slow down the immune response to prevent inflammation
options.D: To provide a rapid and strong defense upon future exposure to the germ

explanation: Exactly! Memory cells never forget a face; they spot the real germ later in life and fight it off instantly. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T12#GNS313_U2_T12_h2)

question: Which family planning method helps protect against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Subdermal implants
options.B: Copper intrauterine devices
options.C: Latex condoms
options.D: Progestin-only pills

explanation: Condoms act as a physical barrier that blocks both sperm and infectious agents. Simple and effective! [learn more](GNS312_U3_T10#GNS312_U3_T10_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a harmful traditional practice affecting reproductive health?

options.A: Female genital mutilation
options.B: Exclusive breastfeeding for infants

options.D: Child marriage

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding is a globally recommended health practice, unlike mutilation or child marriage which cause harm. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h4)

question: When does heavy milk production (known as Lactogenesis II) typically kick in after childbirth?

question: What is a simple, important instruction to give a patient right before the IVP scan starts?

question: Where does home health care primarily take place?

options.A: Inside the patient's place of residence
options.B: At a regional diagnostic laboratory
options.C: Inside a specialized surgical ward
options.D: At a primary health care clinic

explanation: You've got this! Home health care simply means bringing nursing and medical care right to where the patient lives. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS324_U1_T1#GNS324_U1_T1_h1)

question: What physiological event occurs during the resolution phase of the sexual response cycle?

options.C: Pelvic blood flow increases rapidly to prepare for orgasm
options.D: The body gradually returns to its unaroused baseline state

question: You notice on your monthly report that many young clients are skipping their second injectable dose. What is the best action to take?

options.C: Refuse care to any client who misses an appointment date
options.D: Wait until the federal ministry sends a special investigation team

question: What is the term for long-term liver damage caused by repeated inflammation and severe scarring?

question: Why shouldn't patients take erectile dysfunction drugs like sildenafil (Viagra) together with organic nitrates?

question: During a sedated dilation procedure, what are the most critical vital signs for the nurse to keep watching?

options.D: Bowel sound frequency

question: Why is talking about birth control options right after a medical abortion so important?

question: What happens to body cells when a hypotonic IV solution is infused into the vascular system?

question: What is the main goal of selecting patients for home delivery?

question: Which action by a nurse best demonstrates ongoing support for a grieving family after their loved one has passed away?

question: Which patient in a busy emergency ward should a nurse monitor with a pulse oximeter first?

question: What is the main goal of teaching pregnant women about cramps during antenatal visits?

question: What is the main reason health leaders must set clear priorities in a community?

question: What is the medical term for having an abnormally low platelet count, which increases a patient's risk of bleeding?

question: What is the best way to communicate with a patient who has a hearing impairment?

question: Which of these is a leading direct cause of maternal mortality?

question: Why do clinical training programs for PAC providers include values clarification exercises?

question: What does 'mesial temporal sclerosis' mean in temporal lobe epilepsy?

question: A patient develops a sudden, severe facial swelling and rash immediately after starting a new antibiotic. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

question: Which viral infection is most commonly linked globally to unsafe injections?

options.D: Rhinovirus

question: Where does fertilization of the human egg normally happen?

question: A patient lies awake for hours before finally falling asleep. What do we call this?

question: A patient with rapid-acting insulin asks when they should take their injection. What is the best nursing advice?

question: A patient needs an IV that won't get blocked every time they bend their arm. Which spot should you avoid?

question: What happens to carbon dioxide during gas exchange in the lungs?

question: What is the main goal of fire safety when you are caring for a patient in their home?

options.C: Proactive risk reduction to protect clients and nurses

question: What does an apex beat that has shifted far to the left usually suggest?

question: You walk into the ward and notice the fridge storing insulin was unplugged all night. What is the best step to take?

question: In a condition called hemothorax, what main substance builds up in the pleural space?

question: A patient has hearing loss because the sensory hair cells inside their cochlea are damaged. What type of hearing loss is this?

question: What is the primary purpose of the cold chain system?

options.C: Freezing needles and syringes to sterilize them before use

question: Why must nurses pre-test health posters and flyers with the local community before printing thousands of copies?

options.B: To guarantee that the printed posters are waterproof and durable
options.C: To ensure the messages are culturally appropriate and easily understood

question: Why is educating parents about their child's chronic condition so important?

question: Up to how many weeks of pregnancy can a standard medical abortion safely be done?

question: A nurse has three different crushed pill medications to give a patient through a PEG tube. What is the correct way to administer them?

question: Why is it so vital for a nurse to keep a non-judgmental attitude during sexual health assessments?

question: What is the most appropriate initial response when a family member expresses anger toward the nursing staff?

question: You are about to use a sterile pack, but you are not completely sure if the seal was broken. What should you do?

explanation: Well done! Stress triggers hormones that drive blood sugar up, making it much harder for the patient to keep their levels steady. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T2#GNS222_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is the true relationship between FGM and major world religions?

options.A: Christian scriptures require the procedure for moral purity
options.B: FGM is a cultural practice falsely linked to religious texts
options.C: The Holy Quran explicitly commands all families to perform FGM
options.D: Islamic law strictly forbids any form of traditional surgery

explanation: Well done! Major religious books do not command FGM—the link is just a cultural misconception. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T4#GNS312_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why do patients with diabetes need frequent blood sugar checks after an abortion?

options.A: Insulin is no longer effective after surgery
options.B: Physical stress and hormonal shifts cause rapid sugar changes
options.C: Abortion procedures automatically cure diabetes
options.D: Blood sugar levels always drop to zero

explanation: Physical stress and changing hormones make blood sugar levels bounce around, making them much harder to control during recovery. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of occupational health hazard control?

options.A: To reduce the cost of buying new equipment
options.B: To punish workers who break safety rules
options.C: To treat workers only after an accident occurs
options.D: To prevent injuries and illnesses before they happen

explanation: Hazard control focuses on stopping workplace dangers from causing harm in the first place rather than just dealing with the aftermath. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h1)

question: Which action is considered the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Keeping windows closed at night
options.B: Painting isolation walls white
options.C: Frequent and proper hand hygiene
options.D: Changing bed sheets twice a day

explanation: Handwashing with soap and water or using alcohol-based rub removes pathogens from hands before they spread to others. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h7)

question: A mum receiving magnesium sulfate has a breathing rate of 8 breaths per minute and her knee reflexes are gone. What is your very first action?

options.A: Write it down as normal and keep watching.
options.B: Turn up the drip because the dose is too small.
options.C: Tell her to drink plenty of water.
options.D: Stop the magnesium infusion right away and tell the doctor.

explanation: Slow breathing and missing reflexes mean too much magnesium is building up in her body (toxicity)! Stop the infusion immediately and get help—calcium gluconate is the antidote. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h6)

question: When using a bulb syringe to clear a newborn's airway, which part should you suction first?

options.A: Mouth
options.B: Pharynx
options.C: Trachea
options.D: Nose

explanation: Always suction the mouth before the nose! If you do the nose first, the baby might gasp and accidentally inhale any fluid sitting in their mouth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h2)

question: Which type of diseases must be reported the absolute fastest because they can spark sudden outbreaks?

options.A: Routine dental health issues
options.B: Epidemic-prone diseases
options.C: Surgical complication records
options.D: Chronic nutritional deficiencies

explanation: Diseases like cholera or measles move fast! We call these epidemic-prone, and they need immediate reporting so we can protect the community. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary advantage of giving medications through the oral route?

options.A: It bypasses liver metabolism completely
options.B: It is the most convenient and common way
options.C: It guarantees 100 percent drug absorption
options.D: It works faster than intravenous injections

explanation: The oral route is favored because patients can usually swallow pills themselves, making it easy and convenient for long-term care. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h1)

question: A nurse notices morning shift surgical patients report less pain than evening ones. Why is this a good research problem?

options.A: It highlights a noticeable pattern and potential gap in pain management routines
options.B: It proves that evening nurses are performing their duties incorrectly
options.C: It guarantees a promotion for the nurse who records the observation
options.D: It eliminates the need to administer prescribed pain medications

explanation: Spotting differences in patient care across shifts points to a real clinical puzzle worth investigating. You're thinking like a true researcher! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which human sense is widely believed to be the very last to fade when someone is dying?

options.A: Taste
options.B: Hearing
options.C: Sight
options.D: Smell

explanation: Hearing stays active right to the end! That's why we always encourage families to keep talking, praying, and whispering sweet words to their loved one. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T8#GNS221_U4_T8_h7)

question: Why are involuntary reflexes like coughing and vomiting important for survival?

options.A: They increase the amount of red blood cells in circulation
options.B: They cool down the body during a high fever
options.C: They protect the body from harmful substances and blockages
options.D: They help the digestive system absorb extra vitamins

explanation: These protective reflexes quickly expel irritants or foreign items from the airway and digestive tract to prevent injury. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h5)

question: Why does blood from an upper GI bleed usually turn black and tarry (melena) by the time it comes out?

options.A: The patient has been eating too many dark green vegetables
options.B: Bile acids in the large bowel bleach the blood
options.C: Stomach bacteria turn the iron bright red
options.D: Digestive enzymes and stomach acid break down the blood during its trip

explanation: As old blood travels all the way down the long digestive tract, stomach acid and enzymes break down the hemoglobin, turning it dark, sticky, and black. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h5)

question: At the end of life, cells struggle to produce enough of which main energy molecule?

options.A: Adenosine triphosphate
options.B: Glucose
options.C: Hemoglobin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Cells need adenosine triphosphate (ATP) to power their everyday work. When oxygen drops at the end of life, ATP production stops too. You've got this! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T4#GNS221_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why do nurses pre-test IEC materials before launching a campaign?

options.A: To calculate the exact market cost of printing colored paper
options.B: To check if the target audience understands and accepts the materials
options.C: To get official approval from international donor organizations
options.D: To prove to the hospital management that the nurse can draw well

explanation: Pre-testing is like a dry run. It helps you catch confusing designs or misunderstood words before you waste money printing thousands of copies. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T7#GNS124_U5_T7_h4)
